metadata.title: Multiplicatively Weighted Centers of Median Graphs in Quasilinear Time
metadata.description:
A short capped integral-distance threshold transformation converts multiplicatively weighted vertex-center feasibility to additively weighted eccentricities. Combining it with the credited Berge-Ducoffe-Habib additive algorithm and Ducoffe's known implicit optimization mechanism gives a deterministic O(n log^5(2n)) exact-operation algorithm for a center, optimum radius and all centers on every finite connected simple unit-edge median graph supplied by adjacency lists and promised median. This resolves the finite algorithmic form of Open Problem 1 in Ducoffe's Oberwolfach Report 8/2026, without a cube-dimension bound. Nonnegative finite real profiles are allowed in an exact comparison model; no encoding-independent bit bound, graph recognition, arbitrary edge-length, infinite-encoding or local-unimodality result is claimed.

The note credits the earlier cube-free O(n log^2 n) result and makes no novelty claim for the additive algorithm or weighted-median search. Its appendix and verification package give explicit consistent balance-parameter and depth-estimate corrections for two proof issues in arXiv:2410.10235v1, preserving the imported time bound; no claim is made about uninspected final SODA typesetting. Two independent primary-source priority audits found no earlier explicit same-scope resolution, but historical firstness and continued open status are not certified. Inaccessible older tree-center originals, uninspected final SODA typesetting and incomplete indexing bound the audit. The authored-only package preserves original inputs, independent derivations, exact rational finite controls, ordinary nested checksum manifests and an offline replay driver. Brute reference routines are not a fast implementation or an experimental proof of the asymptotic theorem.

whole_publication_original.title: Multiplicatively Weighted Centers of Median Graphs in Quasilinear Time
whole_publication_original.description: An exact threshold reduction gives the optimum weighted radius and all vertex centers of finite unit-edge median graphs in O(n log⁵(2n)) exact operations, with credited algorithms and explicit bit-model limits.
whole_publication_original.abstract: We record a short reduction from multiplicatively weighted center thresholds to additively weighted eccentricities on a graph with bounded integral distances. Combining it with the algorithm of Bergé, Ducoffe and Habib and a known implicit optimization method gives a deterministic O(n log⁵(2n)) algorithm for a center, the optimum radius and all centers of every finite unit-edge median graph. This answers the finite algorithmic form of Open Problem 1 in Ducoffe’s Oberwolfach report, without a bound on cube dimension. The contribution is the threshold observation and its consequence; neither the additive algorithm nor the optimization mechanism is new. We specify the exact comparison model and give explicit corrections to two estimates in the public preprint proof of the imported algorithm.
plain_language: A weighted center chooses a vertex that minimizes the worst weighted distance to every vertex of a graph. A larger weight makes distance to that vertex more costly. Median graphs include trees and hypercubes; every three vertices have a unique median on all three pairwise shortest-path intervals.

This note turns each multiplicative distance threshold into an additive arrival-time problem, then combines credited algorithms to find the exact optimum and every vertex attaining it. The graph may have arbitrarily large cube dimension, and no embedding is supplied.
result: Let G=(V,E) be a finite, nonempty, connected, simple graph with unit edge lengths, n=|V| and shortest-path distance d. Each vertex u has a finite nonnegative real weight w(u). For a candidate vertex x define r_w(x)=max_{u∈V} w(u)d(x,u), the optimum ρ=min_{x∈V} r_w(x), and the full center set C_w={x∈V:r_w(x)=ρ}.

Theorem 1. Given G by adjacency lists, with the promise that G is median, and any such weight profile, a deterministic algorithm computes the exact radius ρ, one vertex in C_w and the entire set C_w in O(n log⁵(2n)) exact operations. No cube-dimension bound or supplied embedding is required. Operations on the original profile only compare bounded integer multiples k w(u), where 0≤k≤n−1.

Zero-weight vertices stay in both the graph and the candidate domain. If n=1 or all weights are zero, the radius is zero and every vertex is a center. The result concerns vertex centers with the original shortest-path distances.

The operation count is an exact comparison model, not an encoding-independent bit-time bound. The optimum can be stored as a pair (k,u) representing k w(u). Overall the search uses O(n log²(2n)) comparisons of original-weight products, in addition to the imported graph operations.

For rational input w(u)=p_u/q_u with positive denominators and numerator and denominator components of at most B bits, comparing k w(u) with j w(v) compares k p_u q_v with j p_v q_u. These integers have O(B+log n) bits; their multiplication and comparison costs, and input reading, must be paid. The additive oracle’s bounded integer labels, including its internal updates, use O(log n) bits. The theorem does not promise unit-cost arbitrary-precision arithmetic or a linear-space oracle.
why_it_works: Put D=n−1. For a nonnegative trial radius R, define b_R(u)=max{k∈{0,…,D}:k w(u)≤R} and a_R(u)=D−b_R(u). When w(u)=0, the budget b_R(u) equals D. Bounded binary search finds each budget using comparisons, without a real-division or unbounded-floor primitive.

For every vertex x and every R≥0, w(u)d(x,u)≤R is equivalent to d(x,u)≤b_R(u), hence to d(x,u)+a_R(u)≤D. Taking all u gives the exact identity {x:r_w(x)≤R}={x:E_{a_R}(x)≤D}, where E_a(x)=max_u(d(x,u)+a(u)). This preserves the whole feasible set, rather than only deciding whether it is empty. Negative radii are infeasible.

The imported Bergé–Ducoffe–Habib algorithm computes all additive eccentricities for a nonnegative integer arrival profile on a median graph in O(n log⁴(2n)) time, including preprocessing. Here 0≤a_R(u)≤D. The short threshold identity works for bounded integral graph distances; the efficient median-graph conclusion uses this credited additive oracle.

The optimum is one of the products k w(u). A known implicit optimization mechanism, credited to Ducoffe, searches the n sorted product rows without materializing their n² entries. The note gives a self-contained comparison-only variant: active intervals include their endpoints, lower row middles are weighted by inclusive interval lengths, and feasible equality is saved in an incumbent with a witness before deletion. These rules cover ties and zero rows. Each step deletes at least one quarter of the active entries, so O(log(2n)) oracle calls suffice; a final query at ρ returns every center.

The already published appendix supplies consistent estimates for the recursion in the named author preprint arXiv:2410.10235v1. It uses f(s)=2⌈log₂s⌉ for s≥3, direct base cases for s≤2, and a fixed-root depth estimate. Both original-arrival and fiber-arrival slice calls are retained. Total child volume at each depth is at most the root order and depth is O(log²n), giving the required additive O(n log⁴(2n)) bound. The appendix credits BDH’s algorithm and structural discoveries; it makes no assertion that the inaccessible final SODA chapter contains the same proof errors.
limitations: The graph is finite, nonempty, connected, simple and unit-edge, supplied by adjacency lists and promised median. Recognition of median graphs, arbitrary edge lengths, continuous facilities along edges and an unspecified encoding of infinite median graphs are outside the theorem. The separate unimodality question in Ducoffe’s report is not settled by this global threshold algorithm.

The accompanying package includes exact reference controls, manuscript source and proof comparisons. Its all-pairs and brute-structure routines check finite cases; they are not a fast general implementation or an experimental proof of the asymptotic bound. Reproduction instructions require normal assertion-enabled execution.

The contribution is the short threshold observation and its consequence. The additive algorithm, implicit optimization mechanism and classical median preprocessing are credited prior work. The bounded literature assessment does not establish worldwide firstness or continued open status at a later date. The appendix’s corrections are explicitly limited to the named public author-v1 proof, whose log-base and product estimates it addresses; no claim about errors in the final SODA publication is made.
background: Ducoffe’s Oberwolfach report asks the finite n-vertex weighted-center algorithmic question, within a discussion that also includes infinite graphs, edge lengths and unimodality. This note answers the finite unit-edge vertex-center form without a cube-dimension bound. It does not claim all the separate questions in that discussion.

Bergé, Ducoffe and Habib provide the additive all-eccentricities algorithm and its median-graph structure. Ducoffe’s ESA 2026 Lemma 2, and Lemma 2.2 of its full author-v1 preprint, already supply the decision-to-optimization mechanism. Classical median algorithms and preprocessing, including the work of Bénéteau, Chalopin, Chepoi and Vaxès, remain dependencies.

For cube-free median graphs, Chalopin, Chepoi, Dragan, Ducoffe and Vaxès already proved the stronger O(n log²n) bound. The present O(n log⁵(2n)) result does not improve that subclass. Algorithms using a supplied tree-product embedding have a stronger representation promise; the unweighted MFCS theorem and the later weighted consequence in the workshop report are not identified as the same statement.
collaboration: Substantive mathematical verification, extensions within a clearly stated model and collaboration toward journal submission are welcome. Authorship should reflect actual contributions. This is a passive invitation; no claim of an existing collaboration is implied.

metadata.title: Multiplicatively Weighted Centers of Median Graphs in Quasilinear Time
metadata.description:
A short capped integral-distance threshold transformation converts multiplicatively weighted vertex-center feasibility to additively weighted eccentricities. Combining it with the credited Berge-Ducoffe-Habib additive algorithm and Ducoffe's known implicit optimization mechanism gives a deterministic O(n log^5(2n)) exact-operation algorithm for a center, optimum radius and all centers on every finite connected simple unit-edge median graph supplied by adjacency lists and promised median. This resolves the finite algorithmic form of Open Problem 1 in Ducoffe's Oberwolfach Report 8/2026, without a cube-dimension bound. Nonnegative finite real profiles are allowed in an exact comparison model; no encoding-independent bit bound, graph recognition, arbitrary edge-length, infinite-encoding or local-unimodality result is claimed.

The note credits the earlier cube-free O(n log^2 n) result and makes no novelty claim for the additive algorithm or weighted-median search. Its appendix and verification package give explicit consistent balance-parameter and depth-estimate corrections for two proof issues in arXiv:2410.10235v1, preserving the imported time bound; no claim is made about uninspected final SODA typesetting. Two independent primary-source priority audits found no earlier explicit same-scope resolution, but historical firstness and continued open status are not certified. Inaccessible older tree-center originals, uninspected final SODA typesetting and incomplete indexing bound the audit. The authored-only package preserves original inputs, independent derivations, exact rational finite controls, ordinary nested checksum manifests and an offline replay driver. Brute reference routines are not a fast implementation or an experimental proof of the asymptotic theorem.

AI tools were used extensively in solving, development, writing, reproduction and adversarial verification. This is an unrefereed preprint with internal AI adversarial reviews; it has not received human peer review or proof-assistant certification.

whole_public_sections_original.title: Multiplicatively Weighted Centers of Median Graphs in Quasilinear Time
whole_public_sections_original.original_abstract: We record a short reduction from multiplicatively weighted center thresholds to additively weighted eccentricities on a graph with bounded integral distances. Combining it with the algorithm of Bergé, Ducoffe and Habib and a known implicit optimization method gives a deterministic O(n log⁵(2n)) algorithm for a center, the optimum radius and all centers of every finite unit-edge median graph. This answers the finite algorithmic form of Open Problem 1 in Ducoffe’s Oberwolfach report, without a bound on cube dimension. The contribution is the threshold observation and its consequence; neither the additive algorithm nor the optimization mechanism is new. We specify the exact comparison model and give explicit corrections to two estimates in the public preprint proof of the imported algorithm.

plain_language: A weighted center chooses a vertex that minimizes the worst weighted distance to every vertex of a graph. A larger weight makes distance to that vertex more costly. Median graphs include trees and hypercubes; every three vertices have a unique median on all three pairwise shortest-path intervals.

This note turns each multiplicative distance threshold into an additive arrival-time problem, then combines credited algorithms to find the exact optimum and every vertex attaining it. The graph may have arbitrarily large cube dimension, and no embedding is supplied.
result: Let G=(V,E) be a finite, nonempty, connected, simple graph with unit edge lengths, n=|V| and shortest-path distance d. Each vertex u has a finite nonnegative real weight w(u). For a candidate vertex x define r_w(x)=max_{u∈V} w(u)d(x,u), the optimum ρ=min_{x∈V} r_w(x), and the full center set C_w={x∈V:r_w(x)=ρ}.

Theorem 1. Given G by adjacency lists, with the promise that G is median, and any such weight profile, a deterministic algorithm computes the exact radius ρ, one vertex in C_w and the entire set C_w in O(n log⁵(2n)) exact operations. No cube-dimension bound or supplied embedding is required. Operations on the original profile only compare bounded integer multiples k w(u), where 0≤k≤n−1.

Zero-weight vertices stay in both the graph and the candidate domain. If n=1 or all weights are zero, the radius is zero and every vertex is a center. The result concerns vertex centers with the original shortest-path distances.
why_it_works: Put D=n−1. For a nonnegative trial radius R, define b_R(u)=max{k∈{0,…,D}:k w(u)≤R} and a_R(u)=D−b_R(u). When w(u)=0, the budget b_R(u) equals D. Bounded binary search finds each budget using comparisons, without a real-division or unbounded-floor primitive.

For every vertex x and every R≥0, w(u)d(x,u)≤R is equivalent to d(x,u)≤b_R(u), hence to d(x,u)+a_R(u)≤D. Taking all u gives the exact identity {x:r_w(x)≤R}={x:E_{a_R}(x)≤D}, where E_a(x)=max_u(d(x,u)+a(u)). This preserves the whole feasible set, rather than only deciding whether it is empty. Negative radii are infeasible.

The imported Bergé–Ducoffe–Habib algorithm computes all additive eccentricities for a nonnegative integer arrival profile on a median graph in O(n log⁴(2n)) time, including preprocessing. Here 0≤a_R(u)≤D. The short threshold identity works for bounded integral graph distances; the efficient median-graph conclusion uses this credited additive oracle.

The optimum is one of the products k w(u). A known implicit optimization mechanism, credited to Ducoffe, searches the n sorted product rows without materializing their n² entries. The note gives a self-contained comparison-only variant: active intervals include their endpoints, lower row middles are weighted by inclusive interval lengths, and feasible equality is saved in an incumbent with a witness before deletion. These rules cover ties and zero rows. Each step deletes at least one quarter of the active entries, so O(log(2n)) oracle calls suffice; a final query at ρ returns every center.

The already published appendix supplies consistent estimates for the recursion in the named author preprint arXiv:2410.10235v1. It uses f(s)=2⌈log₂s⌉ for s≥3, direct base cases for s≤2, and a fixed-root depth estimate. Both original-arrival and fiber-arrival slice calls are retained. Total child volume at each depth is at most the root order and depth is O(log²n), giving the required additive O(n log⁴(2n)) bound. The appendix credits BDH’s algorithm and structural discoveries; it makes no assertion that the inaccessible final SODA chapter contains the same proof errors.
comparison_model: The operation count is an exact comparison model, not an encoding-independent bit-time bound. The optimum can be stored as a pair (k,u) representing k w(u). Overall the search uses O(n log²(2n)) comparisons of original-weight products, in addition to the imported graph operations.

For rational input w(u)=p_u/q_u with positive denominators and numerator and denominator components of at most B bits, comparing k w(u) with j w(v) compares k p_u q_v with j p_v q_u. These integers have O(B+log n) bits; their multiplication and comparison costs, and input reading, must be paid. Recognition of median graphs, arbitrary edge lengths, continuous facilities along edges and an unspecified encoding of infinite median graphs are outside the theorem. The separate unimodality question in Ducoffe’s report is not settled by this global threshold algorithm.

The accompanying package includes exact reference controls, manuscript source and proof comparisons. Its all-pairs and brute-structure routines check finite cases; they are not a fast general implementation or an experimental proof of the asymptotic bound. Reproduction instructions require normal assertion-enabled execution.

The contribution is the short threshold observation and its consequence. The additive algorithm, implicit optimization mechanism and classical median preprocessing are credited prior work. metadata.title: Nonattainment in the Harrell–Stubbe Dirichlet gap inequality
metadata.description:
We prove that the universal Harrell–Stubbe gap bound for Dirichlet eigenvalues is never attained on a nonempty bounded open subset of Euclidean space at any finite index. More strongly, Yang's first inequality is strict at every real threshold above the lowest eigenvalue. The proof uses the classical spectral remainder and a self-adjointness obstruction to finite spectral support of a coordinate times an eigenfunction. No boundary regularity or connectedness is required.

This answers the corrected saturation question recorded in the 2009 Oberwolfach report and listed as OWR-3389-016; the original report's missing square is explicitly documented. The package includes the paper, LaTeX source, independent AI-assisted proof audits, a scoped priority audit, and a dependency-free verifier with 7,016 exact checks. The computation checks algebra and box spectra, not the general analytic theorem. No earlier explicit nonattainment proof was located in the literature checked; this is not an exhaustive priority certification. Research and writing were AI-assisted.

whole_publication_original.title: Nonattainment in the Harrell–Stubbe Dirichlet gap inequality
whole_publication_original.description: The classical Dirichlet eigenvalue gap bound is strict at every finite index, including rough and disconnected bounded regions. Read the complete preprint.
plain_language: For a membrane fixed along its edge, Dirichlet eigenvalues are proportional to squared vibration frequencies. More generally, they describe the Laplacian on a bounded region in any positive dimension.
A classical inequality bounds the gap between consecutive eigenvalues using averages of earlier eigenvalues. This note proves that equality never occurs at a finite index for the Dirichlet Laplacian.
The proof also makes Yang’s first inequality strict at every real threshold above the lowest eigenvalue. It includes disconnected regions, rough boundaries and repeated eigenvalues.
result: Let n ≥ 1 be an integer and let Ω be any nonempty bounded open subset of Rⁿ. Use the Dirichlet Laplacian defined by the energy form on H₀¹(Ω), and list its eigenvalues 0 < E₁ ≤ E₂ ≤ ⋯ with multiplicity. No boundary regularity or connectedness is assumed.

For every integer J ≥ 1, define A_J = (1/J) Σ_{j=1}^J E_j, B_J = (1/J) Σ_{j=1}^J E_j², M₁ = ((n + 2)/n) A_J and M₂² = ((n + 4)/n) B_J. Then M₁² − M₂² > (E_{J+1} − E_J)²/4. Thus the classical gap bound cannot be attained at any finite index.
More strongly, for every real z > E₁, Σ_{E_j<z} (z − E_j)² < (4/n) Σ_{E_j<z} (z − E_j)E_j. These are finite sums over the eigenvalues strictly below z.
Repeated eigenvalues and zero gaps are included. The proof also covers an index ending inside a repeated eigenspace, including the case E_{J+1} = E₁.
why_it_works: The classical commutator trace identity expresses the difference between the two sides of Yang’s inequality as a nonnegative sum over higher spectral modes.

The equality obstruction is short: multiplying a real Dirichlet eigenfunction by a coordinate cannot produce a finite sum of eigenfunctions. If it did, the differentiated eigenvalue equation and self-adjointness would force a derivative vector to vanish, contradicting an integration-by-parts identity. The argument uses the form-defined operator and distributions, so it does not require a smooth boundary.

The high-mode remainder therefore cannot vanish above the lowest eigenvalue. Completing the square in the resulting quadratic inequality then gives the strict gap bound, with multiplicities handled explicitly.
limitations: The theorem concerns the form-defined Dirichlet Laplacian on nonempty bounded open Euclidean sets. Neumann or periodic boundary conditions, unbounded sets and operators with added potentials are different models.

The 2009 Oberwolfach report defines rooted moments M_p but prints M₁² − M₂ in its gap displays. This paper explicitly uses the corrected expression M₁² − M₂², which matches Harrell and Stubbe’s original inequality and scales homogeneously. The negative answer concerns that corrected saturation question.

Finite nonattainment is compatible with sharp leading Weyl asymptotics. It supplies no uniform positive deficit and does not resolve the adjacent quantitative growth question or the separate question about E_J ≤ M_p.

The trace identities and non-strict inequalities are classical and are credited below. The contribution presented here is the explicit nonattainment conclusion and its short equality argument. A bounded source comparison does not certify historical firstness, exhaustive novelty or continued worldwide openness.
Exact algebra and certified box-spectrum checks in the package supplement the analytic proof. They do not machine-prove the theorem for arbitrary domains or provide proof-assistant certification.

metadata.title: Nonattainment in the Harrell–Stubbe Dirichlet gap inequality
metadata.description:
We prove that the universal Harrell–Stubbe gap bound for Dirichlet eigenvalues is never attained on a nonempty bounded open subset of Euclidean space at any finite index. More strongly, Yang's first inequality is strict at every real threshold above the lowest eigenvalue. The proof uses the classical spectral remainder and a self-adjointness obstruction to finite spectral support of a coordinate times an eigenfunction. No boundary regularity or connectedness is required.

This answers the corrected saturation question recorded in the 2009 Oberwolfach report and listed as OWR-3389-016; the original report's missing square is explicitly documented. The package includes the paper, LaTeX source, independent AI-assisted proof audits, a scoped priority audit, and a dependency-free verifier with 7,016 exact checks. The computation checks algebra and box spectra, not the general analytic theorem. abstract.heading: Original abstract
abstract.text: The universal Harrell–Stubbe bound for a gap between consecutive Dirichlet eigenvalues is never attained on a nonempty bounded open subset of Euclidean space at a finite index. This answers negatively the corrected saturation question recorded in the 2009 Oberwolfach report on low eigenvalues. We prove the stronger statement that Yang’s first inequality is strict at every real threshold above the lowest eigenvalue. The proof uses the classical spectral remainder and a short obstruction to finite spectral support of a coordinate times an eigenfunction. No boundary regularity or connectedness assumption is needed.

sections.heading: The idea in plain English
paragraphs: For a membrane fixed along its edge, Dirichlet eigenvalues are proportional to squared vibration frequencies. More generally, they describe the Laplacian on a bounded region in any positive dimension.
A classical inequality bounds the gap between consecutive eigenvalues using averages of earlier eigenvalues. This note proves that equality never occurs at a finite index for the Dirichlet Laplacian.
The proof also makes Yang’s first inequality strict at every real threshold above the lowest eigenvalue. It includes disconnected regions, rough boundaries and repeated eigenvalues.

sections.heading: The precise result
paragraphs: Let n ≥ 1 be an integer and let Ω be any nonempty bounded open subset of Rⁿ. Use the Dirichlet Laplacian defined by the energy form on H₀¹(Ω), and list its eigenvalues 0 < E₁ ≤ E₂ ≤ ⋯ with multiplicity. No boundary regularity or connectedness is assumed.

For every integer J ≥ 1, define A_J = (1/J) Σ_{j=1}^J E_j, B_J = (1/J) Σ_{j=1}^J E_j², M₁ = ((n + 2)/n) A_J and M₂² = ((n + 4)/n) B_J. Then M₁² − M₂² > (E_{J+1} − E_J)²/4. Thus the classical gap bound cannot be attained at any finite index.
More strongly, for every real z > E₁, Σ_{E_j<z} (z − E_j)² < (4/n) Σ_{E_j<z} (z − E_j)E_j. These are finite sums over the eigenvalues strictly below z.
Repeated eigenvalues and zero gaps are included. The proof also covers an index ending inside a repeated eigenspace, including the case E_{J+1} = E₁.

sections.heading: Why the inequality is strict
paragraphs: The classical commutator trace identity expresses the difference between the two sides of Yang’s inequality as a nonnegative sum over higher spectral modes.

The equality obstruction is short: multiplying a real Dirichlet eigenfunction by a coordinate cannot produce a finite sum of eigenfunctions. If it did, the differentiated eigenvalue equation and self-adjointness would force a derivative vector to vanish, contradicting an integration-by-parts identity. The argument uses the form-defined operator and distributions, so it does not require a smooth boundary.

The high-mode remainder therefore cannot vanish above the lowest eigenvalue. Completing the square in the resulting quadratic inequality then gives the strict gap bound, with multiplicities handled explicitly.

sections.heading: Scope, normalization and classical background
paragraphs: The theorem concerns the form-defined Dirichlet Laplacian on nonempty bounded open Euclidean sets. Neumann or periodic boundary conditions, unbounded sets and operators with added potentials are different models.

The 2009 Oberwolfach report defines rooted moments M_p but prints M₁² − M₂ in its gap displays. This paper explicitly uses the corrected expression M₁² − M₂², which matches Harrell and Stubbe’s original inequality and scales homogeneously. The negative answer concerns that corrected saturation question.

Finite nonattainment is compatible with sharp leading Weyl asymptotics. It supplies no uniform positive deficit and does not resolve the adjacent quantitative growth question or the separate question about E_J ≤ M_p.

The trace identities and non-strict inequalities are classical and are credited below. The contribution presented here is the explicit nonattainment conclusion and its short equality argument. A bounded source comparison does not certify historical firstness, exhaustive novelty or continued worldwide openness.
Exact algebra and certified box-spectrum checks in the package supplement the analytic proof. They do not machine-prove the theorem for arbitrary domains or provide proof-assistant certification.
